conflicts: Classification of 417.694, 393.077 and 380.149 nm: the LAC wavelength table assigns them to transitions between excited levels (7 894 - 31 829, 8 759 - 34 192, 7 894 - 34 192); Weber et al. 2022 observe all three by laser excitation from the ground state (upper levels 23 934.20, 25 433.26, 26 297.92 cm^-1) and state that the compilation's assignments are incorrect. The laser classification is entered; the even levels 31 829.03 and 34 192.6 that rest on the old assignments (and the 463.166 nm line 10 244 - 31 829) are not entered.

Level energies of 253Es (LAC database / Worden 1974) and 254Es (laser, 2022) differ by the isotope shift: 28 447.02 vs 28 446.86(5), 28 118.65 vs 28 118.49(20), 28 578.60 vs 28 578.49(20) cm^-1; measured isotope shift of the 351.4 nm line nu(254)-nu(253) = -5.020(54) GHz = -0.167 cm^-1. The 253Es value is energy_cm where the LAC table has the level; for the seven levels missing there the 254Es laser value is energy_cm.
LAC level-table values differ slightly from the 253Es literature energies quoted by Weber et al. 2022 (28 118.65 vs 28 118.58; 28 578.60 vs 28 578.71).

Ground-level B of 253Es: the LAC level table prints -143.8749 (10^-3 cm^-1) but its introduction gives B = -0.1439749 cm^-1; the latter agrees with -4316.254(76) MHz quoted by Nothhelfer et al. 2022 (the table value is a misprint).

J of 17 803.09 cm^-1: the level table gives 15/2, the wavelength table prints 19/2 for the 561.551 nm ground-state line (impossible for an E1 line from J = 15/2); 15/2 is used. The printed wavelength also differs by 7 pm from the level difference.
Ground-state B of 254Es: -6200(300) MHz (2022) disagrees with the earlier single-transition value of the 1999 hot-filament work (shown only graphically in the 2022 paper, not entered).
281.515 nm (0 - 35 507 J=13/2 in the wavelength table) does not fit the tabulated level 35 507.74 (computed 281.546 nm); not entered.
not_found: J of the even levels 25 433.26, 26 297.92, 26 357.00 (laser) and 28 372.78, 28 689.74, 29 159.28, 19 788.32 (LAC): not determined in the sources opened; these levels carry a J text with alternatives, so the pipeline will skip them and the strong lines 342.848, 348.459, 352.349, 379.3, 380.1, 393.1 nm cannot be drawn until a single J is supplied (Wyart, Blaise & Worden, J. notes: Two data sets are merged: (1) 253Es emission-spectrum levels and the strongest classified lines from the archived Laboratoire Aime Cotton database (compilation, no uncertainties printed); (2) 254Es laser resonance ionization (Mainz, 2022): ten first excited states with lifetimes, hyperfine constants and the ionization potential. Lifetimes printed as 30 ns are upper limits (bound). Hyperfine constants taken from the LAC table are converted from 10^-3 cm^-1 to MHz (derived). Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second). relative_intensity is the emission intensity printed in the LAC wavelength table (100 ... 10 000); for the laser lines it was attached by wavelength coincidence (derived matching, see each note).
